q: The cess levied under the Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act on works contracts is:

options.A: 10% of the cost of construction
options.B: 5% of the cost of construction
options.C: 2% of the cost of construction
options.D: 1% of the cost of construction, recovered from the contractor's bills

q: Under the Price Variation Clause of a works contract, the price adjustment payable is computed with reference to:

options.A: The price indices for the relevant components, as specified in the contract
options.B: The actual purchase bills produced by the contractor in all cases
options.C: The rates quoted by the next higher tenderer
options.D: The USSOR rates of the current year

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Events such as war, flood, earthquake or epidemic, which are beyond the control of the parties and prevent the performance of the contract, are treated as force majeure events.
2. On the occurrence of a force majeure event, the period of completion is suitably extended and neither party is liable for damages in respect of the delay so caused.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Contracts governed by the GCC for Services differ from works contracts mainly in that:

options.A: No agreement is executed for services contracts
options.B: They cover the provision of services over a period, paid for periodically as the services are rendered, rather than measurement and payment for items of work executed
options.C: They relate only to the supply of materials
options.D: They are awarded only on nomination, without tenders

q: Where the special conditions of a contract are in conflict with the General Conditions of Contract:

options.A: The General Conditions prevail in all cases
options.B: The contractor may follow either of them at his choice
options.C: The contract becomes void
options.D: The special conditions, having been framed for the particular contract, prevail over the general conditions

q: Tenders received after the due date and time fixed for submission:

options.A: Are treated as late tenders and are not opened or considered
options.B: Are opened and considered if the tenderer has executed works earlier
options.C: Are accepted on payment of a late fee by the tenderer
options.D: Are opened separately after the tender committee meets

q: For submitting bids in e-tendering through IREPS, a tenderer is required to:

options.A: Submit the bid in a sealed cover at the divisional office
options.B: Obtain the prior permission of the tender committee
options.C: Register on the IREPS portal and submit the bid using a valid digital signature certificate
options.D: Deposit the earnest money in cash at the cash office only

q: A work is said to be executed 'departmentally' when it is executed:

options.A: Through another government department
options.B: By the Railway's own staff and labour, without engaging a contractor
options.C: By a contractor engaged on nomination
options.D: Through a public sector undertaking

q: In the Railways, works tenders are examined by a tender committee whose composition varies with the value of the tender:

options.A: All tenders are examined by a single officer
options.B: Higher-value tenders are examined by a two-member committee and lower-value tenders by a three-member committee
options.C: Lower-value tenders may be examined by a two-member committee, while higher-value tenders are examined by a three-member committee including a finance member
options.D: The committee always consists of five members

q: A 'No Claim Certificate' in connection with a works contract is:

options.A: A certificate furnished by the contractor at the time of final settlement that he has no further claims against the Railway under the contract
options.B: A certificate issued by the Railway that the completed work is free from defects
options.C: A certificate issued by the Accounts office that no audit objection is outstanding
options.D: A certificate submitted by unsuccessful tenderers withdrawing their tenders

q: One of the canons of financial propriety is that:

options.A: An authority should not exercise its power of sanctioning expenditure to pass an order which will be directly or indirectly to its own advantage
options.B: Expenditure should be incurred mainly to utilise the budget grant in full before the close of the year
options.C: Public money may be spent freely for the benefit of a particular section of the community
options.D: Allowances should be so fixed as to be a source of profit to the recipients

q: The cost of work-charged establishment engaged specially for the execution of a work is charged to:

options.A: The ordinary revenue (working expenses) head
options.B: The Development Fund
options.C: The contractor executing the work
options.D: The work itself, through the estimate of the work

q: Quantities of earthwork executed on a work are computed from the levels recorded in the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Level Book (field book) maintained for the work
options.C: Contractor's Ledger
options.D: Comparative statement of tenders

q: For a work of small value which is completed in one operation, payment to the contractor may be made through:

options.A: A secured advance bill
options.B: A mobilisation advance
options.C: A first and final bill
options.D: A percentage-rate bill

q: A mobilisation advance granted to a contractor is required to be secured by:

options.A: A personal bond executed by the contractor
options.B: The earnest money deposits of the tenderers
options.C: A mortgage of the contractor's office premises
options.D: A bank guarantee of the requisite amount

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Secured advance is given only against durable and non-perishable materials brought to the site for incorporation in the work.
2. The materials against which a secured advance is given are required to be stored securely, and the advance is recovered as the materials are consumed in the work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The total liquidated damages levied under a works contract cannot exceed:

options.A: 10% of the contract value
options.B: 5% of the contract value
options.C: 15% of the contract value
options.D: 25% of the contract value

q: 'Zonal contracts' on the Railways are:

options.A: Contracts awarded by the Railway Board for all zones together
options.B: Contracts executed exclusively by the zonal workshops
options.C: Annual contracts entered into for the execution of petty works and repairs in a section or zone at pre-agreed rates, avoiding a separate tender for every small work
options.D: Contracts for the supply of stores to the zonal railways

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An overpayment made to a contractor in an on-account bill, if detected later, cannot be recovered from him.
2. On-account (running) payments made to a contractor are in the nature of advance payments, adjustable against the final settlement of the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: If a contractor becomes insolvent or enters into an arrangement with his creditors, the Railway may:

options.A: Continue the contract on the same terms in all cases
options.B: Transfer the contract automatically to his creditors
options.C: Suspend all his payments permanently without terminating the contract
options.D: Determine (terminate) the contract in accordance with the General Conditions of Contract

q: Before determining a contract on account of the contractor's default, the Railway is required to:

options.A: Issue a notice to the contractor calling upon him to remedy the default or failure within the period specified
options.B: Obtain a decree of the civil court
options.C: Forfeit the earnest money deposits of all the tenderers
options.D: Obtain the permission of the tender committee

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The bank guarantee furnished towards performance guarantee or security deposit should remain valid for the period stipulated in the contract, including the claim period.
2. Where the period of a contract is extended, the validity of the bank guarantee furnished under it is also required to be suitably extended.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Contractors for railway works are enlisted or registered:

options.A: For one work only at a time
options.B: In different classes according to the monetary value of works they are eligible to undertake
options.C: Only if they are government departments
options.D: Without any classification, on a single common list

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Orders banning business dealings with a firm, issued by the Railway Board, are applicable across the Indian Railways.
2. A firm can be banned from business dealings without being given an opportunity to show cause against the proposed action.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: An 'Integrity Pact' in connection with a major tender is an agreement between the buyer and the bidders which:

options.A: Fixes the rates to be quoted by all the bidders
options.B: Guarantees the award of the contract to the lowest bidder
options.C: Dispenses with the need for earnest money deposit
options.D: Commits both sides to avoid corrupt practices in the tender process, with oversight by Independent External Monitors

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. If the lowest tenderer does not agree to reduce his rates in negotiation, the Railway should hold negotiations with the next higher (L2) tenderer.
2. If negotiations with the lowest tenderer fail to bring the rates to a reasonable level, the tenders may be rejected and fresh tenders invited.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: While examining the rates quoted in a tender, the rates are ordinarily compared with:

options.A: The rates quoted in the tenders of other railways only
options.B: The personal assessment of the sectional officer
options.C: The Last Accepted Rates (LAR) for similar works and the applicable schedule of rates
options.D: The rates proposed by the contractor in his earlier correspondence

q: For large and complex works, the tender conditions may permit tenders to be submitted by:

options.A: A joint venture of firms, subject to the stipulated conditions and submission of the joint venture agreement
options.B: Individual labourers engaged on the work
options.C: The staff of the Railway serving on deputation
options.D: Only public sector undertakings

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The contractor may fix the rate for an extra item of work entirely at his own discretion.
2. The rate for an extra item is derived, as far as possible, from the rates of similar items already included in the contract; where no similar item exists, it is worked out from the schedule of rates or rate analysis, adjusted appropriately with reference to the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In a works contract, a 'deviation' means:

options.A: A change in the alignment of a new line
options.B: A delay in the completion of the work
options.C: A defect in the materials supplied by the contractor
options.D: A difference between the quantities of items provided in the contract and the quantities actually executed

q: Under the General Conditions of Contract, the arbitrators for deciding disputes arising out of a works contract are appointed from:

options.A: The representatives of the contractor
options.B: The panel of arbitrators maintained by the Railway administration
options.C: The Bar Council of the State
options.D: The tenderers who participated in the tender

q: In a large works contract divided into sections or milestones, liquidated damages may be levied:

options.A: Also for failure to achieve the stipulated intermediate milestones, as provided in the contract
options.B: Only after the expiry of the maintenance period
options.C: At twice the normal rate for each milestone delayed
options.D: Only for delay in the final completion of the whole work

q: Where the completion of a work is delayed for reasons attributable to the contractor and extension of time is granted, the price variation payable in respect of the extended period is:

options.A: Computed with the price indices of the extended period in all cases
options.B: Paid at double the normal rate
options.C: Generally restricted by freezing the indices at those prevailing on the original stipulated date of completion, as provided in the contract conditions
options.D: Decided by the contractor

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A contractor engaging contract labour on a railway work is required to obtain a licence under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, where applicable.
2. The Railway, as principal employer, is required to obtain a certificate of registration under that Act for engaging contract labour through contractors.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In respect of the labour engaged by a contractor on a railway work, compliance with the Employees' Provident Fund and Employees' State Insurance obligations:

options.A: Is entirely optional for the contractor
options.B: Is the direct responsibility of the Railway in all cases
options.C: Is looked after by the tender committee
options.D: Rests with the contractor, and is required to be ensured before his bills are passed for payment

q: On completion of a work, before handing over the site, the contractor is required to:

options.A: Clear the site and remove his surplus materials, plant and temporary structures, restoring the site as required
options.B: Leave his surplus materials and plant at the site permanently
options.C: Sell his surplus materials to the Railway at cost price
options.D: Hand over his plant to the Railway free of cost

q: On receipt of the Letter of Acceptance, the successful tenderer is required to:

options.A: Submit a fresh tender for the same work
options.B: Deposit the earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers
options.C: Execute the formal agreement and commence the work within the period stipulated for the purpose
options.D: Start collecting materials for other works

q: An application by a contractor for extension of the period of completion should ordinarily be made:

options.A: At any time within one year after the completion of the work
options.B: Only after the final bill of the work is paid
options.C: To the tender committee which recommended the tender
options.D: Before the expiry of the stipulated date of completion of the work

q: On-account (running) bills of a contractor for work done are ordinarily prepared:

options.A: At monthly intervals, on the basis of the work measured during the period
options.B: Once only, at the end of the contract
options.C: Only when the contractor demands payment
options.D: After the completion certificate for the work is issued

q: For major projects, investment approval of the competent authority is obtained on the basis of:

options.A: The contractor's tender documents
options.B: A Detailed Project Report (DPR) incorporating the technical details and the financial and economic appraisal of the project
options.C: The completion report of a similar project executed earlier
options.D: The annual Pink Book alone

q: A railway project is ordinarily considered financially remunerative if its anticipated rate of return on the capital invested is not less than:
A project which does not satisfy the normal test of financial remunerativeness may still be sanctioned when:

options.A: It is justified on strategic or socio-economic considerations and is approved by the competent authority on those grounds
options.B: The contractor agrees to bear the loss on the project
options.C: Its cost happens to be below the powers of sanction of the General Manager
options.D: It is included in the Pink Book as a token work

q: 'Viability Gap Funding' (VGF) in a public-private partnership project means:

options.A: A loan taken by the contractor from a bank for the project
options.B: The difference between the estimated cost and the tendered cost of a work
options.C: Capital support or grant provided by the Government to make a socially desirable but financially unviable project viable for private participation
options.D: Funding arranged by the contractor through his own equity

q: The annual capital programme of the Railways presented with the budget broadly comprises:

options.A: Only the list of new lines to be taken up
options.B: The Works Programme, the Rolling Stock Programme and the Machinery & Plant Programme
options.C: The salary budget of the Railways
options.D: The stores procurement programme alone

q: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) was set up by the Railways primarily to:

options.A: Undertake and execute rail infrastructure projects, including through project-specific special purpose vehicles and mobilisation of extra-budgetary resources
options.B: Manufacture rolling stock for the Railways
options.C: Carry on the catering services on trains
options.D: Maintain the accounts of the zonal railways

q: Before the execution of a major railway project is taken up, the statutory clearances applicable to the project, such as environmental clearance where required, are to be obtained by:

options.A: The contractor, after the award of the work
options.B: The tender committee
options.C: The State Pollution Control Board on its own
options.D: The project authority, i.e. the Railways, as part of the processing of the project

q: Land required for a railway project is generally acquired:

options.A: By direct purchase by the contractor executing the work
options.B: By occupation of the land without payment of any compensation
options.C: Through the State Government machinery, with compensation paid in accordance with the applicable land acquisition law
options.D: Only on lease from the private owners of the land

q: On completion of a work, the performance of the contractor:

options.A: Is not recorded anywhere
options.B: Is evaluated and recorded, and unsatisfactory performance can lead to action such as downgrading or banning from future tenders
options.C: Is evaluated by the contractor himself
options.D: Is considered only for the purpose of releasing the security deposit

q: As a general rule, Government (Railway) property is not insured with commercial insurers because:

options.A: The Government bears its own risks (self-insurance), and commercial insurance of its property is generally not considered economical
options.B: Insurance of government property is prohibited by the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Contractors insure all railway property in every case
options.D: The assets of the Railways have no insurable value

q: In e-tendering through IREPS for works:

options.A: Tenderers may submit their offers in sealed covers at the divisional office as an alternative
options.B: The earnest money must be deposited in cash at the cash office in all cases
options.C: Tenders are opened manually in the contractor's office
options.D: Offers can be submitted only online through the portal; manual or physical offers are not considered

q: The Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) published for a work ordinarily indicates:

options.A: Only the name of the work
options.B: The rates at which the work will be awarded
options.C: The brief description of the work, its estimated cost, earnest money, period of completion and the due date and time for submission and opening of tenders
options.D: The names of the contractors who will submit tenders

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where the Railway requests the tenderers to extend the validity of their tenders, a tenderer who does not agree to the extension is entitled to the refund of his earnest money.
2. A tenderer who agrees to extend the validity of his tender cannot, on that account, modify the rates quoted by him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Price variation is payable in every works contract, whether or not a price variation clause is included in the contract.
2. Price variation is payable under a works contract only where the contract expressly provides a price variation clause.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A new railway line can be opened for the public carriage of passengers only after:

options.A: Authorisation by the Commissioner of Railway Safety after inspection of the line
options.B: The completion report of the line is approved
options.C: The first goods train is run on the line
options.D: The expiry of the maintenance period of the works on the line

q: In an EPC (turnkey) contract, payments to the contractor are generally made:

options.A: On the basis of item-wise measurements of every item of work
options.B: Only after the expiry of the defect liability period
options.C: Monthly, as a fixed percentage of the establishment cost
options.D: In stages linked to the completion of defined milestones or activities of the project

q: An approximate (rough cost) estimate for a building work is commonly prepared on the basis of:

options.A: Detailed measurement of each item of work

options.C: The rates quoted by contractors for similar buildings
options.D: The cost of an old building without any adjustment

q: For a proposed new railway line, a rough cost estimate at the survey stage is generally worked out on the basis of:

options.A: Detailed designs of all the structures on the line
options.B: The accepted tender rates of a similar line
options.C: A per-kilometre rate of construction cost applied to the length of the line
options.D: The market value of the land to be acquired

q: The rates in the Unified Standard Schedule of Rates (USSOR) are kept current by:

options.A: Revising them with reference to cost indices reflecting changes in the prices of labour and materials
options.B: Adopting the rates quoted by the lowest tenderers from time to time
options.C: Revising them only when a new Works Programme is prepared
options.D: Leaving them unchanged once they are issued

q: While a proposal for a new work is processed for sanction, the financial appraisal also brings out:

options.A: Only the capital cost of the work

options.D: The additional recurring (revenue) expenditure, such as maintenance and operating costs, that the work will entail after its completion

q: Work-charged establishment sanctioned for a work is:

options.A: A part of the permanent establishment of the Railway

options.D: Maintained for all the works of a division together

q: The engineering survey for a proposed new railway line is carried out by:

options.A: The Engineering (Construction) organisation of the Railway
options.B: The Commercial department of the Railway
options.C: The contractor who will execute the work
options.D: The Railway Protection Force

q: In an item-rate tender, the Schedule of Quantities (Bill of Quantities) forming part of the tender documents shows:

options.A: Only the total estimated cost of the work
options.B: The measurements recorded after completion of the work
options.C: The items of work with their descriptions, units and approximate quantities, against which the tenderers quote their rates
options.D: The names of the approved contractors for the work

q: Before submitting his tender for a work, a tenderer is expected to:

options.A: Obtain the measurements of the work from the Measurement Book
options.B: Negotiate the rates with the Engineer
options.C: Deposit the security deposit for the work
options.D: Visit and inspect the site and satisfy himself about the site conditions, availability of materials and other circumstances affecting the work

q: Where a tender contains abnormally high or abnormally low rates for some items of work, the Tender Committee:

options.A: Must reject the tender in all cases
options.B: Examines the justification for such rates and may call upon the tenderer to justify them before making its recommendation
options.C: Accepts the rates without any examination
options.D: Substitutes the schedule rates for such items on its own

q: For the consideration of a Tender Committee, the executive branch puts up:

options.A: A briefing note summarising the tenders received, the comparative position of the offers and the points requiring decision
options.B: The contractor's ledger of the lowest tenderer
options.C: The completion report of a similar work
options.D: The measurement book of the work

q: If any change in the tender documents becomes necessary before the due date of submission of tenders, it is issued to all concerned by way of:

options.A: A verbal intimation to the known tenderers
options.B: An entry in the Measurement Book
options.C: A corrigendum (addendum) to the tender notice/documents, which then forms part of the tender documents
options.D: A note in the Works Register

q: In e-tendering through IREPS, the earnest money for a tender is furnished:

options.A: Only in cash at the Railway cash office
options.B: By a personal cheque of the tenderer
options.C: After the opening of the financial bids
options.D: Through the modes prescribed in the tender documents, such as online payment or bank guarantee/FDR

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a 'Class-I local supplier' is a supplier whose goods, services or works have local content of:

options.A: 20 per cent
options.B: 50 per cent or more
options.C: 75 per cent
options.D: 100 per cent

q: A composite tender for a work such as a station building is invited when:

options.A: The work comprises components of more than one discipline, such as civil, electrical and signalling works, to be executed together by one agency
options.B: Two different railways execute the work jointly
options.C: The work is to be executed partly departmentally and partly through a contractor
options.D: The tender is invited jointly by the Railway and a State Government

q: In a cost-plus contract, the contractor is paid:

options.A: A fixed lump sum irrespective of the actual cost
options.B: At the rates given in the schedule of rates
options.C: The actual cost incurred on the work plus an agreed percentage or fee towards his overheads and profit
options.D: Only the cost of the materials used on the work

q: Certain matters specified in the General Conditions of Contract are treated as 'excepted matters', in respect of which:

options.A: The decision of the contractor is final
options.B: The decision of the tender committee is final
options.C: The dispute must necessarily be referred to arbitration
options.D: The decision of the Engineer is final and binding on the parties, and the matter cannot be referred to arbitration

q: An arbitral award made under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, unless it is set aside by a court, is:

options.A: Merely advisory in nature
options.B: Enforceable in the same manner as a decree of a court
options.C: Binding only if the contractor agrees to it
options.D: Valid only for one year from the date of the award

q: Under the doctrine of frustration, embodied in Section 56 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a contract becomes void when:

options.A: Its performance becomes impossible or unlawful on account of an event which neither party could prevent
options.B: The contractor finds the work unprofitable
options.C: The rates quoted by the contractor turn out to be too low
options.D: The Railway changes the site of the work

q: The formal agreement executed with a contractor for a work is:

options.A: Executed on plain paper, with no stamp duty payable in any case
options.B: Stamped at the cost of the Railways in all cases
options.C: Executed on stamp paper of the prescribed value, the cost of the stamp paper being borne by the contractor
options.D: Required to be registered with the Sub-Registrar in every case

q: In respect of the earnest money and security deposit held by the Railways under a contract:

options.A: Interest is payable to the contractor at the bank rate
options.B: Interest is payable only on the security deposit
options.C: Interest is payable if the work is completed before time
options.D: No interest is payable by the Railways for the period the amounts remain with them

q: Where a contract is determined on account of the contractor's default, the work already executed by him is:

options.A: Ignored, and no payment is made for it
options.B: Measured and valued at the contract rates, and payment made for it subject to the recoveries and dues of the Railways
options.C: Paid for at the schedule of rates current in that year

q: The measurements recorded in the Measurement Book are signed, in token of their acceptance, by:

options.A: The contractor or his authorised representative, in addition to the official recording them
options.B: The tender committee
options.C: The Accounts Officer alone

q: The completion certificate for a work, recording that the work has been completed in accordance with the contract, is issued by:

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The Accounts Officer
options.C: The Engineer-in-charge of the work
options.D: The Railway Board

q: Unless otherwise specified in the contract, the rates quoted by a contractor for items of work are deemed to be inclusive of:

options.A: Only the cost of labour
options.B: Only the cost of materials at the depot
options.C: The departmental charges of the Railway
options.D: All incidental charges such as carriage of materials to the site, loading, unloading and stacking

q: Under a services contract, where the service rendered by the contractor is deficient, the contract ordinarily provides for:

options.A: Automatic extension of the contract period
options.B: Deduction from the amounts payable to the contractor for the deficiency, as stipulated in the contract
options.C: Forfeiture of the contractor's earnest money in every case
options.D: Termination of the contract without any notice in every case

q: Works which affect the movement of trains on running lines are executed:

options.A: During traffic blocks (possessions) of the line granted for the purpose, or under the prescribed protection

options.C: Only on days when no trains are scheduled to run
options.D: By stopping all train services on the railway indefinitely

q: After completion of track works such as a renewal, trains are initially allowed over the renewed portion:

options.D: The horizontal distance over which the earth is transported and the vertical distance through which it is raised

q: For the purpose of measurement and payment, earthwork in a works contract is classified according to:

options.A: The season in which the work is executed
options.B: The nature of the soil or strata encountered, such as ordinary soil, hard soil and rock, with separate rates for each class
options.C: The type of contract under which the work is executed
options.D: The designation of the officer recording the measurements

q: 'Borrow pits' in connection with a railway work are:

options.A: Excavations made at approved places, generally outside the formation, from which earth is obtained for forming embankments
options.B: Pits dug for testing the quality of concrete
options.C: Storage pits for ballast at stations
options.D: Trenches dug for laying cables along the track

q: In track works executed through a contractor, permanent way materials such as rails and sleepers are generally:

options.A: Purchased by the contractor from the open market
options.B: Supplied by the contractor and charged to the work at his own rates
options.C: Supplied by the Railway and issued to the contractor, who remains accountable for their proper incorporation in the work
options.D: Hired by the contractor from another railway

q: Before the materials brought by a contractor are used on a work:

options.A: They are accepted without any examination
options.B: Their rates are approved by the tender committee
options.C: The contractor's bills for them are paid in advance
options.D: Samples of the materials are got approved by the Engineer, and materials not conforming to the approved sample or the specifications are liable to be rejected

q: In respect of the workmen engaged by him, a contractor is required to:

options.A: Submit their names to the Railway Board
options.B: Maintain registers of the workmen employed, their attendance and the wages paid to them, and produce them for inspection when required
options.C: Deposit their wages with the Railway in advance
options.D: Obtain the sanction of the tender committee for engaging them

q: A contractor executing a railway work is bound to pay to the workmen engaged by him wages not less than:

options.A: The minimum wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 for the employment concerned
options.B: The wages demanded by the workmen
options.C: Half of the wages paid to regular railway staff for similar work
options.D: The wages prevailing in his home district

q: Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, welfare amenities for contract labour at the work site, such as drinking water, first-aid facilities and rest rooms, are to be provided in the first instance by:

options.A: The medical department of the Railway
options.B: The State Labour Department
options.C: The contractor engaging the labour
options.D: The workmen themselves

q: Where a railway project requires diversion of forest land, the project authority is required to:

options.A: Occupy the land on payment of a nominal fee to the forest department
options.B: Obtain the permission of the local panchayat only
options.C: Plant trees within the railway land in lieu of the forest land
options.D: Obtain prior approval for the diversion under the Forest (Conservation) Act and bear the cost of compensatory afforestation and the net present value of the forest land diverted

q: For 'special railway projects', land can be acquired under the special provisions contained in:

options.A: The General Financial Rules
options.B: The Railways Act, 1989, which provides for acquisition of land for special railway projects through the competent authority
options.C: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
options.D: The Works Programme of the Railway

q: Before payment, a contractor's bill is subjected to internal check by the Accounts department, which covers, among other things:

options.A: The sanction for the work, the agreement and the rates, the measurements recorded and the recoveries to be made
options.B: Only the handwriting on the bill
options.C: The attendance of the contractor's labour
options.D: The quality of the contractor's own office records

q: From the amounts payable to a contractor under a works contract, the Railways are required to:

options.A: Deduct a contribution towards the contractor's provident fund
options.B: Retain a part permanently as earnings of the Railways
options.C: Deduct income tax at source, as required under the Income-tax Act, and deposit it with the Income-tax authorities
options.D: Deduct the wages payable to the contractor's workmen

q: Royalty or seigniorage charges payable to the State Government on earth and other minor minerals consumed in a work are, where leviable:

options.A: Borne by the Railways without any recovery
options.B: Paid by the workmen engaged on the work
options.C: Adjusted against the departmental charges of the work
options.D: Recovered from the contractor's bills at the applicable rates

q: The departmental charges recovered from outside parties on deposit works are:

options.A: Retained by the executing division as its own funds
options.B: Credited to the earnings (revenue receipts) of the Railways
options.C: Deposited in the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Refunded to the parties on completion of the works

q: Where a work is executed by one railway on behalf of another railway, the cost of the work is adjusted between the two railways through:

options.A: Inter-Railway Financial Adjustment (IRFA)
options.B: The Contractor's Ledger
options.C: The Stores Suspense account
options.D: The Traffic Book

q: To safeguard railway land against encroachment, the Railways maintain:

options.A: No records of land at all
options.B: Only the completion reports of works executed on the land
options.C: Land plans and records, with the boundaries of railway land demarcated on the ground by boundary pillars or stones
options.D: A register of the contractors who have worked on the land

q: Under the agreement for a private siding, the siding owner is liable to pay to the Railways:

options.A: The salary of the staff of the serving station
options.B: A share of the earnings of the serving station
options.C: The cost of constructing the serving station
options.D: Siding charges for the services rendered by the Railways, such as placement and removal of wagons and haulage within the siding

q: The authority competent to accept a works tender is determined with reference to:

options.A: The designation of the officer who prepared the estimate
options.B: The value of the tender, in accordance with the Schedule of Powers
options.C: The number of tenderers who participated in the tender
options.D: The period allowed for completion of the work
